title: A Smile for the Visitor
premise: Yara Hartwell's late-night call-in show becomes a séance when dead listeners start phoning in, each humming the same incomplete song and asking her to finish it. Her sleep recordings reveal a second voice — the Visitor, an entity that buys survival with signatures — negotiating with the last living resident of a drowned town. Yara must learn the song's final verse from the dead without singing along, because singing it completes the sale. In the end, Yara signs nothing, sings only half the verse aloud to trap the Visitor mid-transaction, and burns the tapes, freeing the residents at the cost of her own voice.
about_author: Zephyrine Zhou is the pen name of a former overnight radio producer who spent six years answering calls from strangers who couldn't sleep. They now write horror in a house with the landline deliberately left connected.

chapters.title: Dead Air, Live Callers
chapters.summary: Yara, hosting the 2 a.m. slot, takes a call from Marisol Vega — who died in the reservoir collapse eight days ago. More dead listeners follow, all humming the same broken song and asking for 'the last verse.' Yara, a compulsive documenter, records everything. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: dread braided with tenderness; she can't hang up on grief, even when it shouldn't be calling.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Reviewing her sleep recordings, Yara hears herself asking questions in a trance — and something answering: the Visitor, courteous and patient, explaining that the drowned town's last resident, Elias Thorn, is days from signing away his neighbors' souls for his own survival. The dead beg Yara to intervene. POV: Yara, interleaved with transcript excerpts. Emotional beat: complicity — she realizes her documentation has been feeding it.

chapters.title: Verse by Verse
chapters.summary: Yara drives to the flooded valley, where Elias, dying and terrified, guards the deed like scripture. The dead teach her the song's verses one by one, each lesson costing warmth, memory, breath — but the final verse no one will speak, because singing it completes any contract within earshot. The Visitor arrives to close the deal. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: love against duty as she chooses the dead over her own safety.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Song
chapters.summary: At the signing, Yara sings the first two verses aloud, forcing the Visitor into the open mid-transaction, then stops — leaving the song forever incomplete, voiding every signature including Elias's. Enraged, the Visitor claims her voice as forfeit. She lets it. The dead cross over singing what she cannot. POV: Yara, ending in silence. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, paid for in the price of survival — hers.
